title: Gabbay's separation theorem
summary:
In mathematical logic and computer science, Gabbay's separation theorem, named after Dov Gabbay, states that any arbitrary temporal logic formula can be rewritten in a logically equivalent past-implies-future form. In other words, the future becomes what must be satisfied.

Gabbay's separation theorem about linear temporal logic with past has proved to be one of the most useful theoretical results in temporal logic. In particular, it enables a concise proof of Kamp's seminal expressive completeness theorem for LTL. Until and Since have the separation property over the natural numbers with the less-than relation, and hence Until and Since are expressively complete over this structure. Until and Since also have the separation property over the real numbers with the less-than relation.

Separation for Linear Temporal Logic was established by Dov Gabbay in 1989. The separation result was produced as a means to establishing a more approachable proof of expressive completeness of temporal languages. Gabbay succeeded in providing a more general route than Kamp, as well as being more accessible.

The separation result is of more interest than just as a tool for improving difficult proofs; it is a result of importance in its own right. For example, it is a basis for creating models which satisfy temporal formulae, and consequently a basis for temporal logic programming.
